description.narrative: Benin Power Compact - Power Sector Reform Project: This project supports the sustainability of Benin's electric power sector through professional regulation, stronger utility operations and private sector participation in generation. description.narrative: Date Outcome of Approval of new tariffs took longer than expected because SBEE wanted to achieve certain service improvements first. These included dealing with a backlog of 22,000 connnection requests and setting up an electronic bill payment system. According to the interim evaluation memo, the revised tariffs were implemented in January 2020 a long side a general government subsidy that effectively shielded all customers from the tariff increases. In December 2020, the GoB instituted a new subsidy that covers the tariff price increase for certain classes of SBEE customers. The subsidy was intended to shield low-income and priority industrial customers from the 15 percent tariff increase. In practice, the targeted subsidy applies to a small proportion of SBEE customers, including business and pre-paid customers who consume less than 500 kwh/month and some large commercial consumers. While the subsidy is not expected to affect SBEE�s long-term financial position, delayed GoB payment of the subsidy to SBEE negatively affects its cash flow in the short-term. As of November 2022, the targeted subsidy is still in place and ARE had completed several steps in the tariff revision process after receiving the necessary inputs from SBEE.
